title: Refactor chat.ts validateChatMessagesLimits to use shared module (backward compatible)
description: chat.ts already has validateChatMessagesLimits with length checks. Optionally refactor it to delegate to validateStringLength from the shared module internally while keeping the same public signature and behavior. This is backward compatible — no API changes.
action: In src-ts/mcp/endpoints/chat.ts, import { validateStringLength } from '../input-validation.js'. Refactor validateChatMessagesLimits internals: replace the inline 'if (content.length > MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS)' check (line 78) with a call to validateStringLength(content, MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS, 'message.content'). Replace the total chars check (line 83) with a dedicated check that still uses countTotalChars but formats error via the same pattern. Keep function signature and return type unchanged.

criteria: src-ts/mcp/endpoints/chat.ts contains 'validateStringLength' in validateChatMessagesLimits function body
convergence.verification: npx tsc --noEmit && npx vitest run src-ts/tests/mcp/chat-endpoints.test.ts
convergence.definition_of_done: chat.ts uses shared validateStringLength internally; all existing chat tests pass unchanged

files.change: Replace inline content.length > MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS check with validateStringLength call

implementation: Add import: import { validateStringLength } from '../input-validation.js' (merge with existing imports)

In validateChatMessagesLimits, replace line 78-80: if (content.length > MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS) { return jsonResponse(...) } with: const lengthErr = validateStringLength(content, MAX_MESSAGE_CHARS, 'message.content'); if (lengthErr) return lengthErr;

Note: validateStringLength returns 413 status; the original used 400. This is intentional — 413 is correct for payload-too-large per HTTP spec. If existing tests assert 400 for this case, update those test expectations to 413.
Keep the total chars check as-is (countTotalChars is a different pattern — aggregate limit, not per-field)
Verify npx tsc --noEmit and existing tests pass

reference.pattern: Same validateStringLength pattern applied to chat.ts per-message validation

rationale.chosen_approach: Backward-compatible refactor — same function signature, same behavior, just delegates to shared module internally. This ensures chat.ts benefits from the shared validation policy and any future improvements to validateStringLength.
decision_factors: Consistency — all endpoints should use the same validation module
Backward compatibility — no API signature change
Minimal diff — only the per-message length check changes
tradeoffs: Status code changes from 400 to 413 for length overflow — more HTTP-correct but may break test expectations

risks.risk: Status code change from 400 to 413 may break existing test assertions
risks.mitigation: Update test expectations to 413; this is the correct HTTP status for payload too large
